rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is nonexistent. This experiment tests a baseline RNA-only model with PCA encoding and singleprofile setting, establishing a baseline accuracy to compare against more complex configurations. It clarifies the impact of RNA encoding and profile settings, which are foundational choices. Starting with a simple model allows subsequent experiments to explore the value of multimodal fusion and other components.

The existing evidence shows that RNA-only singleprofile with pca_n2000 achieves 0.4849 accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile with avgpool aggregation, isolating the effect of profile setting and aggregation. It balances exploration by expanding beyond singleprofile while building on the RNA-only baseline, potentially revealing if multiprofile or aggregation improves performance.

Existing evidence shows that RNA-only multiprofile models (config_002) outperform singleprofile variants. This experiment tests whether replacing avgpool (config_002) with transformer aggregation improves performance, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It builds on the promising multiprofile RNA-only direction while exploring a critical design choice with minimal other changes.

The existing evidence shows that multiprofile with avgpool aggregation (config_002, 0.5906 accuracy) is superior to singleprofile and other aggregation methods. This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (a more sophisticated encoder) while maintaining multiprofile and avgpool settings can further improve accuracy. It isolates the effect of the RNA encoder, a critical design choice, and builds on the promising multiprofile direction with minimal changes.

Existing evidence shows rna_only with scvi_n200 and multiprofile achieves 0.6501 accuracy. This experiment tests whether transformer aggregation (vs avgpool) improves performance for scvi_n200 in multiprofile settings, clarifying if aggregation method is a key factor. It directly builds on the strongest current configuration while isolating a critical design choice.

Existing evidence shows that rna_only with multiprofile, scvi_n200, and avgpool aggregation (config_006) achieves high accuracy. This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder with scgpt (a more advanced model) in the same multiprofile setup improves performance, isolating the effect of the RNA representation. This balances exploitation of the current high-performing rna_only setting with exploration of a potentially better encoder.

The existing evidence shows that RNA-only models with scvi_n200 and multiprofile settings (config_006) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.652970). This experiment tests combining this strong RNA encoder with image data (resnet50) using the same multiprofile and transformer aggregation, but with concat fusion. It isolates the effect of multimodal fusion while building on a proven RNA-only baseline, balancing exploitation of strong evidence with exploration of multimodal potential.

The existing evidence shows that config_032 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer aggregation, concat fusion) achieves the highest validation accuracy so far (0.6878). This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from concat to weighted improves performance, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. It is the best use of the remaining budget to further optimize the top-performing configuration.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_033) achieve the highest validation accuracy so far (0.713). This experiment tests replacing resnet50 with imagenet_vit_l (a more advanced image encoder) while keeping other components the same, to assess if the stronger image representation further improves performance. This clarifies the impact of the image encoder choice, a critical design decision, and leverages the strong prior evidence for scvi_n200 and transformer aggregation.

Existing evidence shows that using imagenet_vit_l as the image encoder with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion achieves high accuracy (config_039: 0.724989). This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder from scvi_n200 to scgpt in this high-performing setup further improves accuracy, isolating the effect of the RNA encoder choice. It is the best use of the final experiment to explore a key design choice with strong potential for performance gains.
